prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the 2010 Manifesto (policy proposals only)

Taxes and public finances
- Raise the income tax personal allowance to £10,000, removing 3.6m low earners and pensioners from income tax; typical gain £700. Fund via: aligning capital gains tax with income tax; restricting pension tax relief to the basic rate; a 1% levy on property value above £2m; per‑plane aviation duty with higher rates for some domestic flights; anti‑avoidance and enforcement; time‑limited “non‑dom” status (up to 7 years).
- Deficit plan: begin cuts from 2011–12 subject to economic conditions; identified savings include a £400 public‑sector pay rise cap for two years, restricting tax credits, ending Child Trust Fund payments, a banking levy, scrapping ID cards/biometric passports/intercept database, cancelling Eurofighter Tranche 3B, prison reform moving from short sentences to community penalties, cutting central inspection regimes, and long‑term changes to defence procurement and public‑sector pensions.
- Create a Council on Financial Stability and conduct a comprehensive spending review with public consultation.

Economy, jobs, business, and banking
- Separate retail and investment banking; introduce a banking levy and reform bonuses; expand local/regional banks, Local Enterprise Funds and Regional Stock Exchanges; ensure state‑influenced banks lend to viable firms.
- One‑year green stimulus to create c.100,000 jobs: refurbish shipyards for offshore wind; £400 “eco cash‑back” for home efficiency/micro‑generation; insulate public buildings; bring 250,000 empty homes into use; bus scrappage scheme.
- Youth/employment: up to 800,000 work placements; 15,000 extra Foundation Degree places; fund adult apprenticeship off‑the‑job costs; raise Adult Learning Grant.
- Establish a UK Infrastructure Bank to mobilise private capital for energy/transport, including high‑speed rail.
- Reduce unnecessary regulation; end “gold‑plating” of EU rules; reform business rates to site value under local control; refocus or replace RDAs; restore a public‑interest test on takeovers; support superfast broadband rollout; use public procurement to grow green markets.
- Support mutuals and co‑ops; postal reform separating Post Office (kept public) and selling a minority of Royal Mail with an employee trust.

Education and skills
- £2.5bn “Pupil Premium” for disadvantaged pupils to cut class sizes and fund one‑to‑one and catch‑up support; improve SEN assessment and teacher training; anti‑bullying measures.
- Independent Educational Standards Authority; slimmed Early Years framework and Minimum Curriculum Entitlement; reform tests and league tables; create a General Diploma blending academic/vocational routes; right for 14–19s to study at college; narrow FE/sixth‑form funding gap.
- Education Freedom Act to reduce central interference; local authorities retain strategic oversight; inclusive admissions for faith schools; more flexible pay.
- Phase out undergraduate tuition fees over six years (final‑year fees scrapped immediately); national bursary scheme; merge skills/HE quangos; rebalance HE/vocational focus.

Health
- Reinvest savings from reduced management, quangos and targets into frontline care (e.g., cancer, mental health, maternity, dementia, prevention).
- Integrate health and social care; guaranteed respite for long‑hours carers; prioritise dementia research; expand access to talking therapies; measures on alcohol pricing/tax; cut air pollution; cancel Heathrow third runway.
- Patient entitlements to timely diagnosis/treatment (with funded alternatives if missed); elected Local Health Boards to replace PCT boards; greater GP choice and access; allow varied providers on a level playing field; duty of candour on errors; robust language/competence checks.

Families, pensions, and consumers
- Shared parental leave and time off for ante‑natal; extend flexible working to all employees; maintain child poverty target; publish anonymised Serious Case Reviews; strengthen Youth Service.
- Restore earnings link for state pension with a “triple lock”; scrap compulsory retirement ages; relax annuity rules at 75; explore a citizen’s pension when affordable.
- Consumer measures: fairer energy tariffs and social tariffs; action on water charge unfairness; curb unfair bank charges; PostBank; cap credit/store card rates after consultation; customer service standards; local retail competition tests; regulated rail fares cut (RPI–1%); clearer airline pricing; fairer parking rules.

Climate, energy, environment, and transport
- Target net zero by 2050; at least 40% electricity from non‑carbon sources by 2020; renewables roadmap; European Supergrid; block unabated coal; no new nuclear; large‑scale home insulation; efficiency targets for public/commercial sectors.
- International: press the EU for a 30% cut by 2020; ETS reform; action on HFCs; fund adaptation; protect forests; illegal‑timber law; product impact labelling.
- Housing: repossession last resort; bring empty homes into use; stronger building standards; enable council housebuilding; retain EPCs but scrap HIPs.
- Transport: invest in local rail by reprioritising from major roads; passenger compensation for rail‑replacement; empower councils on buses; expand cycling/walking; per‑plane duty and cancel SE airport expansions; prepare revenue‑neutral road pricing later; rural fuel discount.

Communities, policing, justice, and immigration
- 3,000 more police funded by scrapping ID cards; cut police bureaucracy; elected police authorities with stronger powers; National Crime Reduction Agency; data‑sharing on knife/gun injuries; night‑bus “stop on request”; better hate‑crime recording; drugs policy based on treatment and independent evidence.
- Justice: prisoners to work and contribute to victim funds; presumption against sentences under six months; move addicts/mentally ill to appropriate settings; expand restorative justice; cancel new prison building.
- Immigration: reintroduce exit checks; create a National Border Force; regional points‑based work system; enforce employer compliance; prioritise deporting criminals; earned citizenship for long‑term law‑abiding residents meeting criteria (with a time cutoff).
- Asylum: independent agency; EU coordination; allow work; end child detention; alternatives to detention; no returns to persecution.

Foreign, defence, and Europe
- Strategic Security and Defence Review; cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B; rule out like‑for‑like Trident replacement; enhance European defence cooperation; improve forces’ pay/housing; reduce MoD overheads.
- Development: enshrine 0.7% GNI aid by 2013; explore transaction taxes and carbon measures for aviation/shipping; reform IFIs; act against corrupt funds/tax havens; focus on health, education, water, social protection, and debt relief.
- Europe: cooperate on jobs, climate, finance, and crime‑fighting; CAP reform; stop Strasbourg travel; budget reform; future in/out referendum on any fundamental change; euro entry only with conditions and referendum.

Political and civil liberties reform
- Proportional voting for MPs (prefer STV) and fewer MPs; votes at 16; fixed‑term parliaments; stronger Commons scrutiny/control of agenda; fully elected second chamber; written constitution via citizens’ convention and referendum; stronger data protection and FOI (including monopoly providers).
- Right of recall; donation cap £10,000 and spending limits; tax‑residency requirements for MPs/Lords/candidates; statutory lobbyist register and tighter rules.
- Freedom Bill: regulate CCTV; curb council surveillance; fairer extradition; protect jury trial and protest; libel reform; end blanket retention of innocent DNA; scrap ID cards/biometric passports/ContactPoint; limit creation of new offences; no mass storage of communications data; retain Human Rights Act.
- Devolution: more powers for Scotland and Wales; needs‑based funding; address England’s position via a constitutional convention; resolve specific Scotland funding issues.
